verdict.root_cause: Platform automation lowered ad's memory limit to 144m at 10:20:21, about five minutes before onset, and it was still in effect with no revert recorded [tr_2df4ae913d06]. Under that cap the ad container is killed and restarted, producing twelve no-traffic intervals in the incident window against zero in baseline [tr_8034c08b4603]. During those gaps frontend's outbound GetAds call fails at connect time — the only error-bearing path across ten traces, a sub-millisecond client leaf with no ad-side server span [tr_0d539ca75829] — surfacing in frontend logs as gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / EHOSTUNREACH to 172.18.0.19:9555 [tr_da6b4d527fda]. Frontend and frontend-proxy alerted only because the error propagates to the edge; frontend's own error ratio is below baseline [tr_8385af5d0deb].
verdict.reasoning: Attribution: traces isolate the single failing path to frontend->ad GetAds while every other dependency and nine of ten traces complete cleanly [tr_0d539ca75829], and frontend's own aggregate errors fell below baseline [tr_8385af5d0deb], so frontend is the noticer, not the culprit. Mechanism: EHOSTUNREACH with a resolved address, no server span, sub-millisecond fail [tr_da6b4d527fda][tr_0d539ca75829] means the ad process was not accepting — excluding slow-dependency and server-side application errors. Why: ad was up and low-error but acquired traffic gaps with no baseline counterpart [tr_8034c08b4603], the signature of repeated kill-and-restart, and the only pre-onset act on any implicated service is the memory cap [tr_2df4ae913d06]. A limit lowered until the process is killed for exceeding it is resource_exhaustion; the fix is restoring the prior limit.
open_questions: No ad-side logs, OOMKill/restart events, or memory-usage metrics were gathered — the OOM mechanism is inferred, not observed.
The no-traffic intervals carry no timestamps, so their clustering near 10:20/10:26 is unconfirmed [tr_8034c08b4603]; the frontend log query also dropped the lines spanning onset [tr_da6b4d527fda].
The 10:03:49 cart protobuf parse failure [tr_da6b4d527fda] is unexplained by this verdict and no cart-scoped dispatch was run.

alternatives.root_cause: Ad lost network reachability from frontend rather than dying — a partition or stale route to 172.18.0.19:9555.
alternatives.why_not: Ad's own traffic gaps show it stopped receiving requests generally, not just from frontend [tr_8034c08b4603], and a partition gives no account of the memory cap landing five minutes before onset [tr_2df4ae913d06].

alternatives.root_cause: A corrupted or unreadable cart store is the real fault, with the ad errors incidental.
alternatives.why_not: The cart parse failure is a single line at 10:03:49, well before onset, and all cart calls in the sampled traces complete without error [tr_0d539ca75829]; it was ruled a distinct failure mode [tr_da6b4d527fda].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring ad's pre-10:20:21 resource_limits (removing the 144m memory cap) should stop the container being killed under the cap, so that: (1) the ad span-metric series stops going undefined — no further no-traffic intervals in the same 5m-rate error-ratio query that showed twelve such intervals versus zero in baseline [tr_8034c08b4603]; (2) frontend stops emitting the repeating gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE / EHOSTUNREACH to 172.18.0.19:9555 lines [tr_da6b4d527fda]; (3) new frontend traces on the ad-serving path carry an ad-side server span under the GetAds client span rather than an error-flagged sub-millisecond leaf [tr_0d539ca75829]. The two prior identical caps were reverted at 02:43 and 07:42 and the quiet periods that followed are the comparison point [tr_2df4ae913d06].
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, more than ~5 minutes after the revert and after the recreate's own connection reset has cleared, frontend still logs gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE/EHOSTUNREACH to port 9555, or the ad error-ratio series still produces undefined (no-traffic) intervals. Note a confounder that cannot be separated by observation here: revert_config recreates the container, so recovery would equally be explained by the recreate alone (stale sticky connection cleared, per the identical-text repeated-error finding in [tr_da6b4d527fda]) rather than by the memory limit. Also note the OOM mechanism itself was never observed — no ad-side logs, OOMKill events, or memory-usage metrics were gathered — so a successful outcome confirms the fix, not the mechanism. Separately, this proposal does not address the 10:03:49 cart protobuf FAILED_PRECONDITION [tr_da6b4d527fda]; if that signature persists or grows after the revert, it is a distinct fault needing its own dispatch.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this is a container recreate of ad for no reason: ad goes dark for the duration, frontend's GetAds calls fail outright during the gap, and any in-process ad cache is discarded. Lifting the memory cap removes a guardrail — if ad genuinely has a memory leak rather than an over-tight cap, it will now grow unbounded and can pressure the host, degrading co-located services instead of failing cheaply in isolation. Because the recreate may assign ad a new container IP, a frontend holding a sticky connection to 172.18.0.19 could keep failing until its channel re-resolves, briefly making things look worse. Finally, the cap was applied by platform-automation on a repeating ~5h cycle [tr_2df4ae913d06]; a manual revert does not stop that automation from re-applying it, so this is symptom relief with a known recurrence, and the automation itself must be addressed outside this system.
proposal.blast_radius: One service recreated: ad. The only inbound caller in this incident's graph is frontend, which sees connection failures on GetAds while the container comes back; that failure propagates through frontend-proxy to the edge, which is exactly the path that alerted [tr_0d539ca75829]. Frontend's other dependencies (cart, checkout, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation) are untouched. Expect a short error blip at the edge before improvement, not a clean step change.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and its proxy simultaneously, with several unexamined downstream dependencies that could be the actual cause. Nothing here can be dismissed as a working system, and no open incident covers it.
